data.title: Inauthentic Account Network Built in Advance
data.summary:
Accounts used in the campaign were created and aged well before the campaign began,
posting innocuous content to establish history before being switched to campaign
messaging.
data.description:
Aged accounts defeat the simplest defences. Platform heuristics and human readers alike
treat account age and posting history as credibility signals, and an operator who invests
months in building them buys past both.

The switch is the artefact worth documenting: a dateable point at which a cluster's
content changes character while its accounts do not. Where several accounts switch within
the same window, that shared timing is substantially stronger evidence of coordination
than anything in the content itself.

Pre-building also dates the operation's planning, which is frequently the most useful
single fact in the report — it establishes that the campaign preceded whatever event it
claims to be responding to.
data.recommendation:
* Date the switch for each account and present the shared timing as the coordination
  evidence.
* Use account creation dates to establish when planning began, and state what that implies
  about claimed spontaneity.
* Report the cluster with its dormant history included; platforms act on the pattern rather
  than on recent content alone.
data.short_recommendation: Date the switch from dormant to campaign content; report the cluster together.
